critic round 3 (narrow confirm, Methodology lens): **REVISE** — one Must-Fix, a real hole in the chain-coverage argument I wrote at v5/v6. Applied at v7; a self-caught stale count applied at v8.

**The round-3 finding.** v6 resolved the c75 backstop reference as breadcrumb-OR-prior-version (an `else` chain). Fallback (2) therefore fired ONLY when no breadcrumb resolved — and that ordering breaks exactly where fallback (2) is supposed to earn its keep. Let round k spawn at S_k and version v_k persist at P_k. On a campaign whose FIRST breadcrumb lands at round j+1 — every campaign straddling the 2026-08-26 mandate landing, i.e. the dominant near-term population by this plan's own 28/2,572 measurement — fallback (1) resolves at v_{j+1} to S_{j+1}, a per-round-tail reference, PREEMPTING fallback (2) with a strictly LATER timestamp (S_{j+1} > P_j). The window (P_j, S_{j+1}) — the inter-round critic-review window, the exact channel this gate exists for — is then covered by no version's check, ever. That reproduces the round-1 defect through the fallback ORDER rather than through the breadcrumb SELECTION. Fix applied: the reference is the MINIMUM of whichever of the two resolve; fallback (2) is a FLOOR, never an else-branch, making every version's window a superset of (P_{K-1}, P_K] unconditionally. Pinned by `test_mixed_breadcrumb_window_still_warns` and success criterion 6(b) — the test that fails if the implementer writes `or` where the spec says `min`.
